cards.text: The word of the LORD comes to Ezekiel, a priest living in the land of the Chaldeans (Ezekiel 1:3). God calls him "Son of man" and opens with a question about the wood of the vine. Friend, I've got my apron on and my ears OPEN.

cards.question: God asks Ezekiel how the wood of the vine measures up against something else. Against what?

answers.text: The branches of the forest trees
The reeds of the Nile river
The stalks of the wheat field

cards.text: Then God gets down to it: can wood be taken from the vine to make something useful? Then He asks about one small, everyday thing.

cards.question: God asks if vine wood could even be made into one small, everyday thing. Which one?

answers.text: A peg to hang utensils on

cards.question: God has been asking what vine wood could be made into. Instead, He says it gets cast into the ___.

cards.text: The fire devours both ends and chars the middle, and God asks if it can be useful for anything now. Friend, that's my first batch the day the oven timer quit: ends GONE, middle black, and me holding up the tray asking, "Can we call this crispy?"

cards.question: True or false: God says that even when the vine wood was whole, before any fire touched it, it still couldn't be made useful.

cards.text: Then it turns. All this talk about vine wood was leading somewhere: "Therefore this is what the Lord GOD says…"

cards.question: Like the vine wood He has given to the fire for fuel, God says He will give up the people of ___.

cards.text: God says He will set His face against them. Not a glance, friend. His FACE.

cards.question: True or false: God says the people of Jerusalem who escape the fire will be safe from then on.
God says that when He sets His face against the people of Jerusalem, something will be known. What is it?

answers.text: That the vine will grow back

cards.text: Last line. God says He will make the land desolate, and He says why. I think this one hurts.

cards.question: God says He will make the land desolate. What reason does He give?

answers.text: The people have lost too many battles
The people have stopped tending the vines
